subject: Agriculture
title: Sterile Insect Technique
description: A quick, practical guide to Sterile Insect Technique.

hook.text: What if you could wipe out a pest by flooding it with mates that can't reproduce? That's the sterile insect technique.

buildup.text: Males are sterilized with radiation, then released by the millions. Females mate with them and produce no offspring.

discovery.text: The US eradicated the screwworm fly from North America using this method in the 1960s—a historic triumph.

twist.text: SIT works best on islands or isolated areas. For widespread pests, the numbers needed are staggering.

climax.text: New genetic versions—using CRISPR gene drives—could make SIT far more powerful, and far more controversial.

punchline.text: Fight pests with pests. Turn reproduction into extinction.

quiz.question: How does the sterile insect technique control pests?
options: Releasing sterilized males that mate but produce no offspring
